elements.title: TOTAL EXTERNAL DEBT STOCK, 2025
elements.description: The headline indicator reports total external debt stock in 2025 and its increase from 2024.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The line shows total external debt from 2015 to 2025. It generally declines from 875.5 in 2015 to 720.5 in 2025, with several fluctuations and a small rise at the end.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 2
elements.title: External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations

data.label: Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type

elements.description: Nested stacked bars break down 2025 external debt into public and publicly guaranteed and short-term debt, then split public debt by creditor type and individual creditors. Multilateral debt is larger than bilateral debt; World Bank-IDA is the largest individual component shown, while other bilateral debt is the smallest.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four panels are labeled External debt / exports, External debt / GNI, Debt service / exports, and Debt service / GNI. Each displays '..' instead of a value; no debt ratios are available for Eritrea.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 3 shows no data values because no debt ratios are available for Eritrea.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two boxes show Official creditors on the left and Private creditors on the right. Each box lists Maturity, Grace period, and Interest rate, with '..' in place of every value.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for official or private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
